consequence: Keyboard and some assistive-technology users cannot reliably expose the Tools, Charts, or Variance links in the global desktop navigation.
problem: Category triggers are non-focusable divs with click handlers and no button semantics, aria-expanded, or keyboard handling; desktop CSS hides submenus until li:hover.
recommendation: Use focusable button-based category triggers with aria-expanded/controls and open submenus on keyboard/focus as well as pointer interaction.

consequence: Equivalent viewport boundaries can drift independently and make cross-page responsive changes harder to reason about.
problem: Across 166 assigned stylesheets, 551 media-query occurrences include 233 literal conditions across 68 distinct literal spellings and 318 token/interpolated conditions across 41 spellings. In particular, max-width 480px appears literally 46 times and max-width 768px 33 times even though vars.scss defines matching mobile/tablet tokens and documents overlapping breakpoint sets.
recommendation: Inventory literal consumers by ownership group, select canonical aliases only for semantically identical boundaries, migrate one group at a time, and verify all three audit viewports before retiring aliases.
title: Breakpoint literals duplicate an already-defined token vocabulary
verification_needed: Coordinator/runtime or cross-workstream corroboration as indicated.
